key_insight: Telescopic Language Models train a single Transformer to serve as a whole continuum of compute budgets, rather than requiring a separate model or compression run for each one. The result is a nested-capacity model that can be deployed at multiple sizes from the same trained artifact.
problem_solved: Deployment often requires different language model sizes for different latency, memory, or cost budgets, but traditional approaches need separate training or distillation for each target point. This paper addresses the inefficiency of maintaining many single-budget models.
method: Train a nested-capacity Transformer using stochastic prefix supervision, where one randomly chosen truncated prefix is trained each step.
Include a full-capacity anchor pass alongside the truncated prefix so the largest model remains well supervised.
Optimize the model so every prefix along the capacity axis can act as a valid language model with next-token prediction.
impact: For practitioners, this can simplify deployment by replacing many model variants with one adaptable model that spans multiple compute budgets. It may reduce training overhead, storage, and operational complexity while improving flexibility at inference time.
